source: rew_tool/intake.py (FIELDS, COUPLINGS) — English is the source; this file only translates

ui.title: Intake — Phase −1
ui.subtitle: First — only what is needed to start measurements. We'll ask for the rest when needed, or read it from the DSP.
ui.legend_prose: asked in session — form doesn't record
ui.couple: asked in a single control together with
ui.probe: checked by the tool, not you
ui.prose_note: The answer lives in prose and in the recorded decision — the form does not write it.
ui.dsp_profile_note: The session will record the answer in the DSP profile together with you
ui.glossary_note: Written to glossary: glossary.json or project.json.glossary
ui.now_why: Car, DSP, its channels, loopback, and who we are tuning for. Pick from options where available. Pre-filled values will be kept as is; change them if yours are different.
ui.auto_title: The tool will determine this — we won't ask you
ui.rows_first: First fill in channels above — rows will appear here.
ui.car_pick: Select a car from the list — fields will fill automatically
ui.car_pick_none: — not in list, will enter below —
ui.car_pick_src: List is from the skill cabin library and adjacent projects. There is no other car catalog in the skill.
ui.car_edited: You changed the selected car — this will be a NEW car, not the one from the list.
ui.dsp_new_hint: This DSP is not in the skill profiles — this is a new DSP.
ui.goal_why: Can be skipped: this will be needed when choosing a target curve and listening tracks.
ui.goal_text: in your own words — what else you want from the system
ui.new_dsp_why: DSP baseline — once: which tiers it has, how many slots in each and how they are labeled, what controls, EQ, crossovers, delays, presets. The channel map on the main page is built from this.
ui.equipment_why: Mainly a description in your own words. The speaker table below is only if you have it documented.
ui.memo_auto: Determined by tool or DSP profile
ui.memo_later: Session will ask or verify on its own when it reaches the step
ui.map_why: One slot per row, like in TCC. Pick a standard code or type your own — the slot switches on by itself; an unused slot is called off-out-A / off-virt-F.
ui.map_first: First select DSP and tiers above — its slots will appear here.
ui.curve_ours: SQ-Comp-Ref — ours, already in skill, no upload needed
ui.curve_ntt_note: Curve file is downloaded there: curves belong to their authors and are not included in the skill.
ui.curve_own_hint: name or file of your curve
ui.dsp_confirm: DSP is changing: {old} → {new}. The old DSP channel map ({n} slots) will be REPLACED with the new one; the old one will remain recorded in the project (dsp.previous_maps), slots are not transferred between DSPs. Save?
ui.map_replaced: These are slots of the new DSP. The saved map of {old} ({n} slots) will be replaced after saving; it will remain recorded in the project, slots are not transferred.
ui.map_new: This is a new DSP: first fill in its baseline separately (link above) — then the map will appear here.
ui.map_new_unsaved: This DSP is not in the skill profiles. Save it — then the separate "New DSP" form will open.
ui.dsp_new_unsaved: New DSP: click "Save", then fill in its baseline in the separate form.
ui.new_dsp_not_new: This DSP has a profile in the skill — its baseline does not need to be asked.
ui.equipment_ph: Speakers, amplifiers, what goes where — as you prefer
ui.knobs_why: Why: a knob in a different position makes two measurement series incomparable. Optional.
ui.knob_name: name, e.g. head unit bass knob
ui.err_no_code: enabled slot without a code — enter a code
ui.err_dup_code: code {code} is already on slot {slot} — one code, one channel
ui.err_fix_first: Nothing saved: fix fields marked in red.
ui.err_still_missing: Nothing new to save. Still missing: {n} — marked in red.
ui.saved_missing: Saved. Still missing: {n} — marked in red.
ui.seat_once: Selected once: cannot be changed after saving.
ui.seat_locked: Cannot be changed: every measurement, delay, and level in this project is made for this seat.
ui.seat_confirm: Target listening position: "{seat}". Cannot be changed after saving — a different seat is done as a copy of the project. Save?
ui.seat_howto: A different seat requires a new project copied from this one (car, DSP, channel map; without measurements). In TCC: "New project" → "from existing" → select seat. Without TCC: tell the skill session "make a copy of the project for passenger" (or another seat).

project.language.ask: Which language to respond in — EN / UK / DE / PL?

project.reviewer_channel.ask: What is the reviewer channel, and is it responding?
project.reviewer_channel.derive: live reviewer test (autosound_ai.py doctor) — response, not setting

project.dir.derive: folder the form is opened for

goal.reference_seat.ask: Who is this project for — driver / passenger / both / all / rear left / rear right?

goal.mode.ask: Tune from scratch, improve existing, or light touch?
goal.mode.derive: method has only one path — tune from scratch

goal.design_path.ask: Virtual-first at the desk, or iterative?
goal.design_path.derive: virtual-first if level 1 + loopback on matching clocks + verified filter model; otherwise iterative

goal.stage_priorities.ask: What soundstage are we building (can't maximize everything)?

goal.constraints.ask: What cannot be touched (doors, trim, budget, time)?

goal.wishes.ask: What else do you want from this system — in your own words?

car.year.ask: Year (optional — describes this specific car and does not classify anything)

source.kind.ask: What plays music (head unit / streamer / phone / …)

source.measurement_input.ask: Which input carries the measurement signal

rew.loopback.ask: Timing reference: physical loopback or acoustic?

rew.api_reachable.ask: Does REW API respond on localhost:4735?

rew.input_clip_checked.ask: Was measurement input checked for clipping?

dsp.readable.ask: Can DSP state be read (dump, screenshot, file export)?
dsp.readable.derive: verified: dump, screen capture, or file export — either works or doesn't

dsp.per_channel_measurable.ask: Can each output be measured individually (solo)?
dsp.per_channel_measurable.derive: always yes: any DSP output can be soloed by muting the rest

dsp.capability_level.ask: Which level is this — 1 full / 2 black box / 3 sum only?
dsp.capability_level.derive: derived from the two answers above

dsp.processing_rate_hz.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly

dsp.tiers.ask: Which tiers does the DSP have (physical outputs, virtual channels, inputs)?
dsp.tiers.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly; otherwise session will ask

dsp.max_count.ask: How many slots does EACH tier have physically? Count the outputs, virtual channels, and inputs of the DSP hardware itself, not just what this car uses — spares are the point of this question
dsp.max_count.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly; otherwise session will ask

dsp.eq.ask: EQ: bands per channel, types (PK / shelves / all-pass), file import and format
dsp.eq.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly

dsp.crossovers.ask: Crossovers: types (LR / BW / BE), orders, independent HPF and LPF
dsp.crossovers.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly

dsp.delays.ask: Delays: step and limits; per-channel polarity; phase control (all-pass)
dsp.delays.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly

dsp.presets.ask: Presets: how many; what gets reset on preset switch (input!)
dsp.presets.derive: from built-in DSP profile if model matches exactly

dsp.measurement_input.ask: Input routing: is there a dedicated input for the measurement signal?

channel_map.glossary_agreed.ask: Channel codes and naming grammar agreed AND recorded?

channel_map.tier.ask: Which tier does this slot belong to

channel_map.role.ask: What it powers (woofer / mid / tweeter / sub / …)
channel_map.role.derive: from channel code (w- woofer, m- mid, tw- tweeter, sw sub)

channel_map.descr.ask: How this channel is labeled in the DSP software
channel_map.descr.derive: read from DSP software when importing its current state

channel_map.fs_hz.derive: from driver datasheet — by make and model

channel_map.routing.ask: Which outputs does each VIRTUAL channel feed?

channel_map.hardware_controls.ask: Remote knobs and switches outside DSP (SubRC / RearRC / bass knob) and where they are set

target_curve.genres.ask: What do you listen to? (select multiple)

target_curve.loves_most.ask: What do you love most in sound?

target_curve.loudness.ask: How loud do you usually listen?

target_curve.track_library.ask: Which test track libraries do you have? (select multiple)

dsp.tiers_used.ask: Which DSP tiers will be used?

hardware.description.ask: Describe other equipment in your own words (speakers, amplifiers, anything)

when.install: before first sweep, during install check (phase −1, step 6)
when.0: in phase 0 — during measurement session and after baseline measurement, when choosing target curve
